title: Walkthrough index
lede: The Pages site now lists every merged walkthrough at `walkthroughs/`, instead of a 404, and stops shipping the template as if it were one.

files.question: When does the index get built?
files.summary: The copy step now calls `site.js`, still on `main` only, between the app build and the Pages upload.
files.owns: Running the site step on pushes to `main`.
files.tested: Not run in CI yet: the step runs only on a push to `main`. The same command was run locally.

files.question: Which pages ship, and how is the list made?
files.summary: Copies `NNNN-*.html` pages to the output folder and writes `index.html` from each page's spec.
files.owns: Picking numbered pages, reading `title` and `issue`, ordering, escaping.
files.never: Builds or checks walkthroughs; `build.js` and `check.js` do.
files.tested: `site.test.js`: order, escaping, a missing issue, and that the template is left out.

steps.title: push to main: the site step runs
steps.explain: The step replaces the old `cp *.html`, which also copied `template.html`. It still skips pull requests, like the upload it feeds. Not run in CI yet: the first push to `main` after this merge proves it.

run.from: - name: Add walkthroughs to the site

steps.title: site.js picks the pages and copies them
steps.explain: Only names like `0004-move-notes.html` match, so `template.html` stays out. Each page's title comes from its JSON spec, which every walkthrough commits next to its HTML. Running `node docs/walkthroughs/site.js <dir>` on `main`'s files wrote 8 pages plus `index.html`.

steps.title: the index is written
steps.explain: Sorting names in reverse puts the highest issue first, because names start with the zero-padded issue number. Pages with no issue (`0000`) come last. Titles are escaped because spec text could contain `<`. A page with no issue gets no `#` tag.

notes.title: Generated at deploy time, not committed
notes.detail: A committed index would need updating in every PR and would conflict between PRs. The counter-argument is that nobody can see the index before merging. Running `site.js` locally shows it.

notes.title: Ordering of `0000` pages
notes.detail: Pages with no issue sort by reverse name, not by merge date. Ordering by merge date would need git history at deploy time, which is not worth it for this list.

omitted.docs/walkthroughs/site.test.js: Tests for `site.js`, described in its `tested` field.
